messages:
ashok: Heads-up — after the batching-heuristic change landed on main we see a ~18% tail-latency regression on 8xA100 multi-GPU runs. Pasted perfetto slice + nsys summary below, need help triaging. links: perfetto://run/abc123, s3://redwood-perf/nsys/1795.tgz

liam: can you paste the high-level symptom? throughput drop or latency tail?

ashok: throughput is roughly same, p50 okay, p95/p99 up. timeline shows periodic GPU idle gaps between pipeline stages. NCCL traces show collectives starting in sequence (serialized) rather than overlapping.

maria: that smells like collective kickoff ordering — maybe host-side enqueue or stream sync changed. Any kernel selection changes around the same CL?

ashok: yes, kernel selection default bumped to `fused_attn_v2` when seq_len > 2048, and the batching coalescer now groups micro-batches into variable-sized micro-batches (to reduce kernel launches). suspect interaction: larger fused kernel has higher setup/setup-host overhead and that delays sequence leading to sequential NCCL launches.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: rollout 2026-03-01T17:22 by @deploy-team — batching-heuristic v3.1 enabled in canary

liam: shared a short perfetto excerpt: `GPU0: compute 12.2ms -> AllReduce kickoff 0.6ms -> idle 4.7ms -> compute 10.9ms` repeated. NCCL ops appear to be issued from the same host thread in quick succession.

maria: can you run nsys with CUDA API and NCCL tracing? e.g.:
```
nsys profile --capture-range cudaProfilerApi --trace=cuda,nvtx,nccl -o /tmp/run1795 %CMD%
```
and capture the host-side call stacks for `ncclAllReduce`?

ashok: yes running now. quick grep from nsys summary: `ncclReduceScatter: mean 0.8ms, skewed start times across ranks by up to 5ms` — perfetto flame shows rank0 issues start first then rank1..rank7 follow with small gaps causing 1-2x pipeline bubble.

liam: hypothesis: kernel selection change increases kernel launch latency on the leader GPU which holds up the schedule of subsequent NCCL launches. Also kv-cache miss path triggers extra host syncs? Any evidence of KV cache invalidation at those times?

ashok: good catch — traces correlate a KV cache refresh (~host RPC + weight remap) right before the largest bubble. KV miss handler does a `cudaMemcpyAsync` then `cudaStreamSynchronize` on the default stream (ugh). That sync can stall host thread ordering for NCCL launches.

maria: two actionable experiments to isolate: (1) disable the new fused_attn selector and pin old kernel (fast path) to see if launch latency drops; (2) run with NCCL_PROTO=LL and NCCL_ALGO=tree to force different collectives ordering and see overlap change. Also try setting `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=0` and ensure all KV copies use dedicated streams + events instead of default stream sync.

liam: add `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO` + capture `NCCL_P2P_LEVEL=SYS` run too. I'll script automated nsys+perfetto collection across 8 ranks and produce a table of allreduce start offsets per rank.

ashok: plan: I'll rollback kernel selector toggle in canary and re-run today, Maria please prototype KV-copy-on-stream patch, Liam produce per-rank start-offsets. If rollback fixes it we'll need a micro-benchmark to measure kernel launch overhead and gating cost.

perf-bot: perf-alert: p99 latency increased by 17% on `canary-a100-8g` starting 2026-03-01T17:23 — linked traces uploaded to s3://redwood-perf/alerts/1795/

maria: quick snippet we can try to avoid host sync:
```
// use dedicated stream + event
cudaMemcpyAsync(dst, src, n, cudaMemcpyDeviceToDevice, kv_stream);
cudaEventRecord(copy_done, kv_stream);
// later, instead of cudaStreamSynchronize(default)
cudaStreamWaitEvent(nccl_stream, copy_done, 0);
```
should let nccl ops proceed without blocking host thread ordering.

ashok: perfect. will run the rollback + kv-stream patch in separate runs and attach nsight timelines. thanks all. :thumbsup:

liam: if rollback shows improvement, also consider queuing NCCL launches on a dedicated comm-thread to avoid any accidental host-side sync coupling.

maria: noted — I'll open a PR for the KV-stream change and add a micro-benchmark for kernel-launch overhead measurement.

ashok: assigning: liam (nsys capture + per-rank offsets), maria (kv-stream PR + microbench), ashok (rollback + comparison). will reconvene after both runs finish.

liam: ack, starting captures now.
